newsitem.title: UK: Stocks edge lower in London.
newsitem.headline: Stocks edge lower in London.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 index stalled, weighed down by disappointing results from a couple of large blue chip companies and continued strength in the pound. The benchmark index finished 3.4 points lower at 4,304.3, with decliners narrowly outpacing advancers 51 to 47.

FRANKFURT - Germany's IBIS DAX index ended sluggish trade slightly higher, with little volume around to forge any significant new gains, but dealers said the DAX index would likely clear the 3,200-point hurdle soon. A half-day pre-Lent holiday in Frankfurt meant that volumes were thin and the IBIS DAX, which gauges electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended the day at 3,191.45 points. Earlier the DAX index ended floor trade at 3,187.58 points, up 3.22 points or 0.10 percent.

PARIS - Stocks finished slightly weaker in a consolidation prompted by Wall Street's drop on Monday, but takeover speculation livened trading in financial shares. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 13.28 points, or 0.51 percent, at 2,582.09.

ZURICH - Stocks overcame a midday dip to end above the 4,400-point mark in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index for the first time. The closing level of 4,408.4 points was also an all-time high and the ninth consecutive record close on the Swiss bourse. The broad Swiss Performance Index also hit a new high, adding 11.91 points, or 0.43 percent, to 2,808.04.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market was closed today for the National Foundation day holiday. On Monday the key 225-share Nikkei average gained 314.13 points to close at 18,181.17.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended sharply lower, dragged down by weak futures and continued selling pressure on the property sector. The Hang Seng Index fell 189.33 points, or 1.39 percent, to close at 13,454.21.

SYDNEY - The share market edged its way to a fractionally firmer close with soft finishes offshore having little impact as local players focused squarely on upcoming interim profit results. The All Ordinaries index added 1.7 points to 2,448.1.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended slightly firmer but well off their highs in heavy trading, knocked by a weak rand which reacted poorly to comments from central Reserve Bank Gov. Chris Stals. The overall index gained 19.0 points to 6,975.0 points, industrials added 6.6 points to 8,293.1, and golds lifted 7.9 points to 1,358.3 points.
